report.incidentSummary: At Indian market open (09:15 IST / 03:45 UTC), stock order traffic surged tenfold to ~48,912 orders/min (~815 orders/s), exceeding the external broker API's order rate limit of 400 req/s. The broker API responded with HTTP 429 Too Many Requests, which triggered automated retries from broker-connector and order-service, further magnifying load. Once retry attempts were exhausted, order-service rejected orders with HTTP 503, causing order placement success rate to drop to ~72-76% (~24% failure rate). order-service CPU spiked to ~87% due to handling the 10x burst and retries, but did not saturate or time out. As opening traffic subsided below 400 req/s around 04:12 UTC (09:42 IST), rate limiting ended and order success normalized to >99%.
report.rootCauseStatement: The incident was caused by external broker-api order rate limiting (quota: 400 req/s) being overwhelmed during market open by legitimate user order volume reaching ~815 req/s (48,912 orders/min). The resulting HTTP 429 Too Many Requests responses from broker-api, compounded by automated retries, caused order-service to reject ~24% of orders with HTTP 503 after retries were exhausted. order-service CPU elevation (~87%) was a consequence of the traffic spike and retry handling, not a capacity bottleneck.

hypotheses.cause: External broker API order rate limit (400 req/s) was exceeded by legitimate market-open order burst (~815 orders/s), triggering HTTP 429 rejections that were exacerbated by unthrottled retries, causing order-service to fail ~24% of orders with HTTP 503 after retries were exhausted.
hypotheses.rationale: Directly proven by broker-connector HTTP 429 logs and metrics confirming rate limits on /orders, order-service 503 rejection logs explicitly citing broker 429 rate limit after retries, and the timing of recovery matching traffic dropping below 400 req/s.

hypotheses.cause: order-service internal capacity saturation (CPU / worker thread exhaustion) causing order processing timeouts and failures at market open.
hypotheses.rationale: Reporter's suspicion ruled out. Although CPU reached 86.68% and thread pool warnings were emitted, order-service latency p95 peaked at 681.9 ms (far below timeout limits), connection pools were not saturated, and all 231 errors were explicit rejections from broker 429s after retries, with zero timeouts or crashes. High CPU was a symptom of processing 10x traffic and retry loops.

hypotheses.cause: Software deployment regression or rate limit configuration change in order-service or broker-connector.
hypotheses.rationale: No deployments, configuration changes, or rollbacks were performed on order-service or broker-connector preceding the market open.

facts.statement: External broker-api returned HTTP 429 Too Many Requests ('limit 400 req/s; retry-after 1s') to broker-connector on the POST /orders endpoint starting at 2026-10-12T03:45:00.705Z through 2026-10-12T04:11:57.035Z.
order-service logged 231 errors rejecting orders with HTTP 503 stating 'order <ref> rejected: broker rate limit (429) after 2 retries' between 03:45:40Z and 04:11:49Z.

order-service incoming order rate surged tenfold from 6,440 orders/min (~107 orders/s) at 03:44Z to 48,912 orders/min (~815 orders/s) at 03:45Z at market open, remaining above 20,000 orders/min until after 04:00Z.
broker-connector request_rate peaked at 1,061 req/s at 03:45Z and stayed near or above 400 req/s until 04:11Z, while rate_limited_count peaked at 1,049/min isolated entirely to the /orders endpoint.

order-service error_rate rose from 0.3% to 19.51% at 03:46Z, order_success_rate dropped from 99.2% to 71.96-76.02%, and both fully normalized to baseline (0.5% error rate, 99.14% success rate) at 04:12Z.

order-service CPU peaked at 86.68% at 03:46Z, latency p95 peaked at 681.9 ms (well below the 2,000 ms broker-connector timeout), and database connection pool usage peaked at 41.87 out of 100 with lock wait under 5 ms.
broker-connector retry_count surged from normal levels (<5/min) to between 216/min and 464/min during the rate-limiting window (03:46Z - 04:11Z).
No deployments, configuration changes, or infrastructure modifications occurred on order-service or broker-connector in the days preceding or during the incident.

assumptions.statement: External broker-api operates with a per-second sliding-window or leaky-bucket rate limiter that enforces exactly 400 req/s across our account.

recommendedActions.verification: Confirm contractual quota upgrade with the broker and verify broker-connector throughput exceeds 400 req/s at 09:15 IST without encountering 429 errors.

The resulting HTTP 429 Too Many Requests responses from broker-api, compounded by automated retries, caused order-service to reject ~24% of orders with HTTP 503 after retries were exhausted. order-service CPU elevation (~87%) was a consequence of the traffic spike and retry handling, not a capacity bottleneck.
